title: Salsa Roja
subtitle: cooked red tomato salsa with chilli and cumin
excerpt: Salsa roja is the all-purpose cooked tomato sauce of Mexican cooking. It is used as a dipping sauce, a base for enchiladas, a topping for eggs, and a condiment for tacos. This version is simple and reliable, built from tinned tomatoes, onion, chilli, and cumin.
sourceNotes: Salsa roja is a staple of Mexican cooking used daily in homes and restaurants across the country. The cooked version keeps well and has a deeper, more rounded flavour than raw salsa.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double or triple. Useful to have in the fridge or freezer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.

content.text: Blend until as smooth or textured as you like. A fully blended salsa is more versatile for cooking with. A rougher texture is better for dipping.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, chilli flakes, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes, vinegar, and salt. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thickened. Blend to your preferred texture.
Taste and adjust salt and chilli. Cool and store in a jar.

items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar or a little more tomato to balance.
Continue simmering uncovered until it reaches the thickness you want.

content.text: Salsa roja is the everyday cooked tomato sauce of Mexico. It is made in homes and restaurants across the country and used in dozens of ways -- as a base, a topping, a dipping sauce, and a cooking medium. The cooked version has a deeper, more mellow flavour than raw salsa and keeps far longer. It is one of the most useful things to have in the fridge.
